title: Merging two copies: union by id, newest `at` per record, `gone` against the same or older `at` only, the hybrid clock, `told` never changing
written_in: SCHEMA_V3 0 and 2.3; DECISIONS_ROUND2 D4, H1, H6, H9, L (merge q1 to q8), M3 to M5, N1, N2, O2, O3, Q5, Q7, S3, AB watch (restoring a backup with the cloud on), AD8 (the shared ui keys restored with a new at), AE1 (keyed overrides merged key by key), AE2, AE5 (restore with the D4 clock, every list, held marks, keyed overrides, a 38.31-format backup), AF3 (ui keys removed per key) and AG1 (a write after a restore never ties with it)
notes: Every amount is made up and in whole minor units (yen).
Times are hybrid clock values written as ISO with the time zone offset (section 0). They are compared as moments, never as text: 10:00+09:00 is 01:00 UTC, 02:30+01:00 is 01:30 UTC.

Question `next_at`: the `at` a device writes, the larger of now and (newest seen + 1 ms), in now's offset; a now more than a day ahead of the newest seen is held at the newest seen + 1 ms [L merge q8]. Question `next_at_warn`: the same, with whether the warning is shown. Question `came_back`: the records removed in `mine` that the merge brings back [L merge q4]. Each record may carry `by`, the device part of its last writer [L merge q1]; `steps` and `rules` entries carry their own `at` [L merge q2]; shared `ui` carries `ui.at`, one `at` per key [L merge q6]; the copy's `rev` after a merge is the larger of both plus one [L merge q3]. A `steps` or `rules` entry is removed by its own `gone` with its own `at`, and is settled like a record: newer `at`, then `gone`, then the larger `by` [M3]. Entries carry their own `by` beside their `at`, and shared `ui` keys carry theirs in `ui.by` beside `ui.at` [M5]. Question `receive`: a copy that arrives is merged in after every `at` in it more than a day ahead of the newest `at` the receiving device has seen is held at that point plus 1 ms, with the warning [M4]; the `devices` syncs do the same. Question `newer`: which of two times is later. Question `merge`: two copies merged, lists ordered by id. Questions `merge_symmetric` and `merge_same`: whether merging A with B gives the same as B with A, and whether merging a copy with itself changes nothing. Question `devices`: a short story of edits and syncs on two devices, and the record one device ends with.

A copy held on arrival is marked `held: { came, at }`: the `at` it came with and the `at` it was held at (a `ui` key's mark is in `ui.held`). A record held once keeps its held `at`: a copy whose `at` is the mark's `came` counts at the held `at`, so the fast device takes the held value when the merged copy comes back, and its copy arriving again is not held a second time [N1]. `told` is held the same way as `at` [N2]; the earliest `told` is then kept, so the first held one stays.

Ids [O2, O3]: question `id_for` builds the id of a record the app writes for a known moment (`set:<occurrence>`, `auto:<schedule>@<due>`, `pe:<the occurrence that started the period>:<place>`, `ps:<the occurrence it stands in for>` [T1]), so two devices writing the same moment make one record and the merge keeps the newest `at`; a `devices` edit may give `make` (what the record is) instead of `id`. Question `id_ok`: whether an id has the shape section 0 gives, `<device part>-<session part>-<counter>` with a 10-character session part, or is a built id.

Ids [Q5, Q7]: `id_for` also builds `rm:<place>` (the move to Waiting written when a place with money is removed), `close:<account>` (the closing's transfer or write-off; with several records `close:<account>:1`, `:2`, in order, `n` giving the number [S3]) and `skip:<occurrence>` (the skip written when a self-logged spend is removed). So the same removal, closing or skip written on two devices is one record.

cases.question: next_at
cases.title: The clock is ahead of everything seen: `at` is now

cases.question: next_at
cases.title: Now equals the newest seen: one millisecond later
cases.why: max(10:00:00.000, 10:00:00.000 + 1 ms) = 10:00:00.001, so a new write is always newer than anything this device has seen.

cases.question: next_at
cases.title: A slow clock: newest seen plus one millisecond
cases.why: This device's clock says 09:05 but it has seen a record at 10:00. max(09:05, 10:00:00.001) = 10:00:00.001, so its edit still counts as newer than what it saw.

cases.question: next_at
cases.title: Two time zones: compared as moments, written in this device's offset
cases.why: now is 01:30 UTC; newest seen is 01:15 UTC, + 1 ms = 01:15:00.001 UTC. now is later, so `at` is now, written with this device's +01:00.

cases.question: newer
cases.title: The later moment can be the smaller text
cases.why: a is 01:00 UTC, b is 01:30 UTC, so b is newer, although as text "...T02:30" sorts before "...T10:00". Comparing `at` as text would let the wrong copy win.

cases.question: merge
cases.title: Union by id: a record on each device, both kept
cases.why: Different ids, so both are in the union [D4]. Nothing is dropped.

cases.question: merge
cases.title: The same record edited on both: the newer `at` wins
cases.why: 10:05 is newer than 10:00, so the copy with 1,500 wins [D4].

cases.question: merge
cases.title: The winner's fields, the oldest `told`
cases.why: theirs wins on `at` (10:05), so a is 1,500. `told` is never taken from the winner: the oldest seen for the id is kept, 12:00 not 12:30 [H1, 2.3].

cases.question: merge
cases.title: An Undo newer than the other copy wins
cases.why: The removed copy's `at` (21 Nov 10:05) is newer than the other's (20 Nov 12:00): gone wins, with its goneBy.

cases.question: merge
cases.title: `gone` wins a tie on `at`
cases.why: Both `at` are 21 Nov 10:00:00.000. H6: a copy with `gone` wins against one whose `at` is the same or older, so the removed copy wins before any device tie-break.

cases.question: merge
cases.title: A Redo (newer, not gone) wins over the Undo it reverses
cases.why: The Redo cleared gone and goneBy and moved `at` to 10:01, newer than the Undo's 10:00. `gone` wins only against the same or older `at`, so the Redo wins [H6].

cases.question: merge
cases.title: Removed on one device, edited later on the other that never saw it: the edit wins
cases.why: H6: the removed copy (10:00) is older than the edit (10:05), so `gone` does not win and the edited record comes back with 1,350. L merge q4 confirms it: an edit newer than a removal brings the record back, and the next check-in shows "came back" (mg-30).

cases.question: merge
cases.title: A removed record on one device only is kept, still removed
cases.why: Nothing is deleted (section 0): a removed record stays in the union with its `gone`, so a third copy that still has it alive cannot bring it back unless that copy is newer.

cases.question: merge
cases.title: The same amount typed on two devices: the merge keeps both
cases.why: Two ids, so both stay. The merge never removes either; the possible double is offered to the person (matching double-01) [H9, 2.3].

cases.question: merge
cases.title: A schedule changed on both devices: the steps merge by `from`, neither step is lost
cases.why: Entries inside `steps` carry their own `at` and merge by `from` [L merge q2]. The 1 Nov step is the same on both; the 1 Dec step (typed on this device at 10:00) and the 1 Apr step (typed on the other at 10:05) are each on one side only, so both are kept, in date order. The rest of the record comes from the newer copy (10:05). Before L the whole newer record won and the December step was lost.

cases.question: merge
cases.title: A single record (`home`): the newer `at` wins
cases.why: Single records carry `at` (section 0) and merge the same way: 10:05 is newer, so minBank is null (no minimum).

cases.question: merge
cases.title: A field this page does not know stays on the winning copy
cases.why: theirs wins on `at`; unknown fields are kept (section 0), so `colour` from a newer page survives the merge.

cases.question: merge
cases.title: Lists inside the plan merge by id too
cases.why: `plan.budgets` entries are list records with id, told and at (section 0), so they are a union by id like events.

cases.question: merge
cases.title: Two time zones: the later moment wins, not the larger text
cases.why: mine is 01:00 UTC, theirs 01:30 UTC (the laptop is in Europe). theirs is newer and wins with 1,250 (mg-05).

cases.question: merge_symmetric
cases.title: Merging A into B gives the same as B into A
cases.why: Every rule above picks a winner from the two copies alone (newer `at`, then `gone` on a tie, oldest `told`), never from which side is "mine". So both devices end with the same copy: e1 removed, e2 at 950, e3 kept.

cases.question: merge_same
cases.title: Merging a copy with itself changes nothing
cases.why: Each record meets an identical copy of itself; any rule keeps it as it is. A merge sent again after a cloud conflict (2.3) therefore cannot change anything twice.

cases.question: merge_symmetric
cases.title: Same `at`, both alive, different amounts: both devices still agree
cases.why: "The device part breaking ties" (section 0) means the tie is decided by something both devices see the same way, so both end with the same record. Which one wins is in mg-26 (the larger `by`) [L merge q1]; this case only checks that they agree.

cases.question: devices
cases.title: A phone whose clock is a day fast is held back to what it has seen
cases.why: A's clock says 24 Nov 10:00, 25 hours after the newest `at` it has seen (23 Nov 09:00): more than a day ahead, so its edit is held at 23 Nov 09:00:00.001 and a warning is shown [L merge q8]. B syncs, then edits at 23 Nov 10:05 (its own clock, later than anything it has seen), so 1,800 wins on both devices with `at` 23 Nov 10:05. `told` never moved. Before L the fast clock wrote 24 Nov 10:00 and pushed B's edit to 24 Nov 10:00:00.001.

cases.question: devices
cases.title: The same fast phone no longer wins against a later edit made without seeing it
cases.why: A's edit is held at 23 Nov 09:00:00.001 (its clock is more than a day past the 09:00 it has seen) [L merge q8]. B edits offline at 23 Nov 10:05, later, so 1,800 wins on both devices. Before L the fast clock's 24 Nov 10:00 beat B and 1,500 won.

cases.question: devices
cases.title: A record made on one device and edited on the other keeps its first `told`
cases.why: The record is made on A at 12:00, so `told` is 12:00. B's edit at 18:00 moves `at` to 18:00 and changes the amount, but never `told` (section 0, H1). So a check made at 15:00 that day still holds this spend, wherever it was edited.

cases.question: merge
cases.title: The same `at` on both, both alive: the larger `by` wins
cases.why: Both copies have `at` 21 Nov 10:00:00.000 and neither is removed. Each record carries `by`, the device part of its last writer; on an equal `at` the larger `by` wins [L merge q1]: bbbbbb is larger than aaaaaa, so 1,200 wins on both devices.

cases.question: devices
cases.title: An edit writes the device part of its writer in `by`
cases.why: The record was made on A (its id starts aaaaaa) and last written on B at 18:00, so `by` is bbbbbb, the device part of its last writer [L merge q1]. The id still names the maker; `told` stays at 12:00 (H1).

cases.question: merge
cases.title: The same step edited on both devices: the newer entry wins
cases.why: Both copies hold a step from 1 Dec. Steps merge by `from`, each by its own `at` [L merge q2]: 10:00 is newer than 09:30, so the 260,000 step wins.

cases.question: merge
cases.title: The copy's `rev` after a merge is the larger of both plus one
cases.why: The copy's `rev` is the larger of both plus one [L merge q3, q5]: 9 + 1 = 10. e1 is the same on both, so its `at` does not move: a record's `at` moves only when it changes [L merge q3].

cases.question: came_back
cases.title: An edit newer than a removal brings the record back, and the check-in can say so
cases.why: e1 was removed here at 10:00 and edited on the other device at 10:05: the newer edit brings it back, so the next check-in shows "came back" for e1 [L merge q4]. e2's copy on the other device (09:00) is older than the removal, so e2 stays removed.

cases.question: merge
cases.title: Shared `ui` keys merge one by one, by `ui.at`
cases.why: Shared `ui` keys carry their `at` in `ui.at` [L merge q6]. main: 10:05 (theirs) is newer than 10:00, so free. sb: 10:10 (mine) is newer than 10:00, so 1. win is only on theirs, so 3. Each key keeps the `at` it won with.

cases.question: merge
cases.title: A copy from an older page with no `told`: the one there is kept
cases.why: mine wins on `at` (10:05) but has no `told`. The earlier `told` is kept, and the only one there is theirs, 20 Nov 12:00 [L merge q7, H1].

cases.question: next_at
cases.title: A clock two days ahead of what the device has seen is held at the newest seen plus one millisecond
cases.why: now is 48 hours after the newest `at` seen, more than a day ahead. It is held at that point plus one millisecond: 23 Nov 10:00:00.001 [L merge q8].

cases.question: next_at_warn
cases.title: The held `at` comes with a warning
cases.why: As mg-33, and a warning is shown that this device's clock is ahead [L merge q8].

cases.question: next_at_warn
cases.title: Exactly one day ahead is not more than a day: `at` is now, no warning
cases.why: now is 24 hours after the newest seen: a day ahead, not more, so `at` is now and nothing is held [L merge q8].

cases.question: merge
cases.title: A step removed on one device stays removed, even when the other device edited the schedule later
cases.why: The record: 10:30 (theirs, the new name) is newer than 10:20, so the name is theirs. The steps merge by `from`, each by its own `at` [L merge q2]. The 1 Jan step was removed here by its own `gone` at 10:20 [M3]; theirs is the step as it was at 10:10, older, so the removal wins and stays in the list as a removed entry. The union cannot bring it back, and the next merge finds the same `gone`.

cases.question: merge
cases.title: A step removed and edited at the same `at`: the removal wins, as on a record
cases.why: An entry is removed by its own `gone` with its own `at` [M3], so it is settled the way a record is: the newer `at`, then on the same `at` the copy with `gone` [H6], then the larger `by` [M5]. Both steps have `at` 10:20, so the removed one wins although bbbbbb is the larger `by`. The record itself ties on `at` too and neither is removed, so the larger `by`, bbbbbb, gives its fields [L merge q1].

cases.question: receive
cases.title: A copy that arrives more than a day ahead of what this device has seen is held
cases.why: The newest `at` this device has seen is 23 Nov 09:00, so a day ahead is 24 Nov 09:00. The clock cap applies to a copy that arrives too [M4]: e1's 25 Nov 10:00 is more than a day ahead, so it is held at 23 Nov 09:00:00.001, marked with the `at` it came with and the held one, and the warning is shown [L merge q8, N1]. e2's 23 Nov 20:00 is less than a day ahead and is kept. Then the merge: held e1 (09:00:00.001) is newer than mine (08:00), so 1,500 wins; `by` stays cccccc, its last writer.

cases.question: devices
cases.title: A new phone two days fast: its edit is held when it reaches the other device, and a later edit there wins
cases.why: A is new and has no `at` of its own seen, so its own write is not held: 25 Nov 10:00. When A's copy reaches B, whose newest seen is 23 Nov 09:00, the record is more than a day ahead and is held at 23 Nov 09:00:00.001 and marked `held: { came: 25 Nov 10:00, at: 23 Nov 09:00:00.001 }` [M4, N1]. B's edit at 23 Nov 10:05 is later than anything B has seen, so it is written at 10:05 by bbbbbb and wins: 1,800; the edit keeps the mark (mg-42 shows why). Before M4, B took in 25 Nov 10:00 as seen and its edit was pushed to 25 Nov 10:00:00.001.

cases.question: merge
cases.title: Two steps with the same `from` and the same `at`: the larger `by` wins
cases.why: Each entry carries its own `by` beside its `at` [M5]. Both 1 Dec steps have `at` 10:00 and neither is removed, so the larger `by` wins: bbbbbb, 255,000, on both devices. Before M5 the larger sorted text won, which was 260,000.

cases.question: merge
cases.title: Two `ui` keys with the same `at`: the larger `by` in `ui.by` wins
cases.why: A shared `ui` key carries its `by` beside its `at`: `ui.by` beside `ui.at` [M5, L merge q6]. main has the same `at`, 10:00, on both, so the larger `by` wins: bbbbbb, trip. Before M5 the larger value as text won, which was waiting.

cases.question: devices
cases.title: A record held once keeps its held `at`: the fast copy that arrives again does not beat the later edit
cases.why: A writes 1,500 at 25 Nov 10:00 (A has seen nothing, so nothing is held). On B, whose newest seen is 23 Nov 09:00, a day ahead is 24 Nov 09:00, so the record is held at 23 Nov 09:00:00.001 and keeps the mark `held: { came: 25 Nov 10:00, at: 23 Nov 09:00:00.001 }` [M4, N1]. B writes 1,800 at 10:05, later than 09:00:00.001, so it wins; an edit keeps the mark (unknown fields are kept, section 0). A's copy arrives again, still 25 Nov 10:00. B's newest seen is now 10:05, a day ahead is 24 Nov 10:05, so before N1 it was held again at 10:05:00.001 and beat B's edit (1,500 on both). Now its `at` is the one B already held, so it takes the held 09:00:00.001 [N1]: 09:00:00.001 is older than 10:05, and 1,800 stays.

cases.question: devices
cases.title: The fast device takes the held value when the merged copy comes back, so the later edit wins there too
cases.why: As mg-42 up to B's edit: B holds 1,800 at 23 Nov 10:05 with the mark `held: { came: 25 Nov 10:00, at: 23 Nov 09:00:00.001 }`. B's copy reaches A. A's own copy is 1,500 at 25 Nov 10:00, which is the `came` of the mark, so A takes the held value, 09:00:00.001 [N1]. B's 10:05 is newer, so A shows 1,800 by bbbbbb, the same as B. Before N1 A's 25 Nov 10:00 was newer than 10:05: A kept 1,500 and B's edit was lost.

cases.question: devices
cases.title: With no edit in between, the fast device ends with the held `at` too
cases.why: B holds A's 25 Nov 10:00 at 23 Nov 09:00:00.001 (newest seen 23 Nov 09:00 plus 1 ms) and marks it [M4, N1]. When B's copy comes back, A's own `at`, 25 Nov 10:00, is the mark's `came`, so A takes the held value: 1,500 at 23 Nov 09:00:00.001, still by cccccc, its writer [N1]. Both devices now hold the same `at`, so any later edit on B (10:05, say) is newer on both.

cases.question: merge
cases.title: Merging the fast copy with the held one: the mark decides, in either order
cases.why: Mine is the fast device's 1,500 at 25 Nov 10:00. Theirs is B's 1,800 at 23 Nov 10:05, carrying `held: { came: 25 Nov 10:00, at: 23 Nov 09:00:00.001 }`. Mine's `at` is the `came`, so it counts as 09:00:00.001 [N1]; 10:05 is newer, so theirs wins whole, mark and all. `told` is 20 Nov 12:00 on both. Before N1 the newest `at` was 25 Nov 10:00 and 1,500 won.

cases.question: receive
cases.title: A `steps` entry held once keeps its held `at` when the same fast copy arrives again
cases.why: This device held the fast copy's 25 Nov 10:00 once, at 23 Nov 09:00:00.001, on the record and on its 1 Jan step, and then edited both at 10:05 (the marks stay). The same fast copy arrives again. Its `at` on the record and on the step is the `came` of the marks, so each takes its held 09:00:00.001 [N1, M5], not 10:05:00.001 (newest seen 10:05 plus 1 ms). 10:05 is newer on both: the name and 275,000 stay. Nothing new was held, so no warning: the warning was shown when it was first held.

cases.question: merge
cases.title: A shared `ui` key held once keeps its held `at`, with its mark in `ui.held`
cases.why: A `ui` key carries its `at` in `ui.at` and its `by` in `ui.by` [L merge q6, M5], so its mark is in `ui.held` beside them. Theirs is the fast device's 25 Nov 10:00, the `came` of mine's mark, so it counts as 23 Nov 09:00:00.001 [N1]. Mine's 10:05 is newer: trip stays. Before N1 25 Nov 10:00 was newer and waiting won.

cases.question: receive
cases.title: A record made on a fast device: its `told` is held the same way as its `at`
cases.why: e3 was made on a device two days fast, so its `told` and `at` are both 25 Nov 10:00 (H1: `told` is set when the record is made). Newest seen here is 23 Nov 09:00, a day ahead is 24 Nov 09:00, so both are held at 23 Nov 09:00:00.001 [M4, N2] and the warning is shown. Before N2 `told` stayed 25 Nov 10:00, so e3 came after every check on 23 Nov whatever its real order. The `at` keeps its mark [N1].

cases.question: devices
cases.title: The held `told` is kept when the fast copy arrives again and when it goes back
cases.why: A makes e2 at 25 Nov 10:00: `told` and `at` both 25 Nov 10:00. On B (newest seen 23 Nov 09:00) both are held at 23 Nov 09:00:00.001 [M4, N2]. B edits at 10:05: `at` moves, `told` never does [H1]. A's copy arrives again: its `at` is the mark's `came`, so 09:00:00.001 [N1]; its `told`, 25 Nov 10:00, is more than a day past B's newest seen (10:05), so it is held at 10:05:00.001, and the earliest `told` is kept: 09:00:00.001 [H1, L merge q7]. Back on A, its own `told` 25 Nov 10:00 against 09:00:00.001: the earliest, 09:00:00.001, so the record keeps its held `told` on both. B's 10:05 edit (900) wins on A as in mg-43.

cases.question: id_for
cases.title: A settlement the check-in writes is named by its occurrence
cases.why: Ticking Pay at the check-in settles pay@2026-12-25, so the event it writes is `set:pay@2026-12-25` on every device [O2].

cases.question: id_for
cases.title: A spend that logs itself is named by its schedule and date
cases.why: The gym fee's own spend for its 1 Feb occurrence is `auto:gym@2027-02-01`, whichever device writes it [O2]. The date is the occurrence's due date before any move, as in every occurrence name [H2].

cases.question: id_for
cases.title: A period-end answer is named by the pay that started the period and its place
cases.why: The answer for what was left in Free to spend in the period begun by pay@2026-11-25 (it ended Thu 24 Dec) is `pe:pay@2026-11-25:free` [O2, T1]: a period is named by the occurrence of its pay, never by a day that can move.

cases.question: id_for
cases.title: A period started without the pay is named by the pay it stands in for
cases.why: A period start the person chose for Sun 20 Dec, standing in for the pay due Fri 25 Dec, is `ps:pay@2026-12-25`; the day they chose is its `date` [O2, N5, T1].

cases.question: devices
cases.title: Jun and Tess each tick Pay on their own phone: one record, the newest `at`
cases.why: Both ticks settle pay@2026-12-25, so both phones write `set:pay@2026-12-25` [O2]. The merge joins them as one record: Tess's 248,000 at 08:02 is newer than Jun's 250,000 at 08:01, so it wins; `told` keeps the earliest, 08:01 [L merge q7]. Bank: 50,000 + 248,000 = 298,000, never 548,000.

cases.question: merge
cases.title: The two copies of the ticked pay merge into one event
cases.why: One id, so one record: newest `at` wins (248,000), earliest `told` kept (08:01) [O2, D4, L merge q7].

cases.question: merge
cases.title: The gym spend written on the phone and on the laptop is one spend
cases.why: The phone (offline) wrote the gym fee's spend at 07:10 and the laptop at 09:30, both as `auto:gym@2027-02-01` [O2]. One record after the merge: the laptop's `at` is newer; the earliest `told` (07:10) is kept. Bank: 100,000 - 8,000 = 92,000, never 84,000.

cases.question: merge
cases.title: Both phones start the new period on the same day: one `periodStart`
cases.why: Each phone answered "start the new period on 20 Dec"; both write `ps:pay@2026-12-25` (the pay it stands in for) [T1] [O2, N5], so the merged copy holds one: newest `at` (09:05), earliest `told` (09:00).

cases.question: id_ok
cases.title: An id with a ten-character session part
cases.why: Device part 6 characters, session part 10 random characters (letters and digits), counter 41 [O3].

cases.question: id_ok
cases.title: An id with the old three-letter session part is not made any more
cases.why: Three letters give 17,576 session parts: a phone opened 3 to 5 times a day reuses one 34 to 95 times a year, and the same session part with the counter from 1 gives the same ids (final_review_1 finding 3). The session part is 10 random characters [O3].

cases.question: id_ok
cases.title: An id built from what the record is
cases.why: Records the app writes for a known moment are named by what they are, not by device and session [O2].

cases.question: merge
cases.title: Two page opens on one device never share ids: Monday's lunch and Thursday's rent both stay
cases.why: Each page open draws its own 10-character session part [O3], so counter 1 on Monday and counter 1 on Thursday are different ids, and the merge keeps both (final_review_1 S5 lost the 1,200 lunch).

cases.question: id_for
cases.title: A removed place's move to Waiting is named by the place
cases.why: Removing the trip writes the move of its money to Waiting with the id `rm:trip` on every device [Q7], so two devices removing it make one move.

cases.question: id_for
cases.title: A closing's transfer or write-off is named by the account
cases.why: Closing the old bank writes its transfer out (or the write-off of what cannot be moved) as `close:old` [Q7].

cases.question: id_for
cases.title: The skip a removed self-logged spend writes is named by its occurrence
cases.why: Removing the gym fee the app logged for its 8 Feb occurrence writes `skip:gym@2027-02-08` [Q5], whichever device does it.

cases.question: id_ok
cases.title: Built ids rm:, close: and skip: are ids
cases.why: `rm:<place>` is a built id [Q7].

cases.question: id_ok
cases.title: A closing's built id
cases.why: `close:<account>` is a built id [Q7].

cases.question: id_ok
cases.title: A skip's built id
cases.why: `skip:<occurrence>` is a built id [Q5].

cases.question: merge
cases.title: A goal removed on the phone and on the laptop before they sync: one move to Waiting, not two

cases.question: restore
cases.title: AB watch: restoring an older backup with the cloud on writes `gone` with a new `at` for what is newer and gives the backup's records a new `at`
cases.why: A backup saved Tue 10 Nov holds a spend of 1,000, a spend of 3,000 and the pay schedule (250,000 from 1 Nov). After it, with the cloud copy on, the desktop changed the 1,000 to 1,500 (15 Nov), added a spend of 2,000 (16 Nov), removed the 3,000 (17 Nov) and added a pay step of 260,000 from 1 Dec (18 Nov). On Sat 21 Nov at 09:00 the phone restores the backup. The restore [AB watch]: the 2,000 spend is not in the backup, so it is written `gone` (the restore's day, 21 Nov) with `at` 21 Nov 09:00 and `by` phn001; the 1,000 spend and the 3,000 spend are the backup's, so they come back as the backup holds them (1,000, and the 3,000 with no `gone`), each with `at` 21 Nov 09:00. The pay schedule is the backup's with a new `at`; its 1 Nov step is the backup's with a new `at`, and the 1 Dec step, newer than the backup, is removed by its own `gone` with its own new `at` [M3]. `told` stays the first one each record had [H1].

cases.question: restore_merge
cases.title: AB watch: the merge with the cloud copy keeps the restore, on either side
cases.why: A backup saved Tue 10 Nov holds a spend of 1,000, a spend of 3,000 and the pay schedule (250,000 from 1 Nov). After it, with the cloud copy on, the desktop changed the 1,000 to 1,500 (15 Nov), added a spend of 2,000 (16 Nov), removed the 3,000 (17 Nov) and added a pay step of 260,000 from 1 Dec (18 Nov). On Sat 21 Nov at 09:00 the phone restores the backup. Each restored record and step has `at` 21 Nov 09:00, newer than every `at` in the cloud copy (the newest is 18 Nov 10:00), so per record and per step the restore wins [D4, M3]: the 1,000 spend at 1,000, the 3,000 spend back, the 2,000 spend and the 1 Dec step gone. `told` is the earliest seen, the same on both sides. Merged either way round it is the restored copy. Before this rule the union merge brought every newer record back at the next sync, so a restore rolled nothing back.

cases.question: restore
cases.title: AD8: a restore gives the shared `ui` keys a new `at` too
cases.why: The backup (Tue 10 Nov) holds two shared screen answers, askNums true and noDebts true, each stamped 10 Nov 10:00 by the phone. After it the desktop changed askNums to false (15 Nov 10:00). On Sat 21 Nov 09:00 the phone restores the backup: each shared `ui` key takes the backup's value with a new `at`, 21 Nov 09:00, and `by` phn001 in `ui.at` and `ui.by` [AD8], as the records do [AB watch].

cases.question: restore_merge
cases.title: AD8: the merge with the cloud copy keeps the restored `ui` keys, on either side
cases.why: The cloud copy still has askNums false at 15 Nov 10:00. The restored key is stamped 21 Nov 09:00, newer, so it wins per key [L merge q6, AD8]: askNums true. noDebts is true on both sides; the restored stamp (21 Nov 09:00) is the newer, so its `at` and `by` are kept. Merged either way round it is the restored `ui`. Before AD8 the restore kept the backup's old `at` (10 Nov), so the cloud's false came back at the next sync.

cases.question: merge
cases.title: AE1 (e1): a one-occurrence amount set on the phone survives a rename on the desktop before they sync
cases.why: Mako, offline on the phone at 10:00, sets December pay to 0 (unpaid leave): `amounts` key 2026-12-25 with its own `at` 10:00 and `by` phn001. At 10:05 he renames the pay on the desktop, which never saw the key. The record goes to the newer copy, the desktop (10:05): name "Salary (Acme)". The keyed override merges key by key like `steps` [AE1]: 2026-12-25 is only on the phone, so it stays. December counts 0, not 300,000. Before AE1 the newer record won `amounts` whole and the 0 was lost (confirm_review_3 item 1).

cases.question: merge
cases.title: AE1 (e1): a budget line's `once` set for different periods on two devices keeps both
cases.why: The phone sets Food for the period of the 25 Dec pay to 70,000 (a family visit) at 10:00; the desktop sets the period of the 25 Jan pay to 20,000 at 10:05. Each `once` key carries its own `at` and `by` and merges key by key [AE1]: two different keys, so both stay. The record's own fields go to the newer copy, the desktop (10:05). Before AE1 only the desktop's January key survived.

cases.question: merge
cases.title: AE1 (e1): a loan's planned extra payments (`extraSteps`) added on two devices keep both
cases.why: The phone plans 30,000 extra on the car loan from 1 Jan (10:00), the desktop 10,000 from 1 Apr (10:05). `extraSteps` entries merge by `from` like `steps` [AE1]: both stay, so January to March pay 30,000 extra and from April 10,000 (the latest entry started). Before AE1 the newer record won the list whole and January's payment was counted 30,000 too low.

cases.question: merge
cases.title: AE1: the same key on both devices goes to the newer key; a key removed on one device stays removed
cases.why: Both copies hold January's 20,000 from 1 Nov. The phone sets December to 70,000 at 10:00 and removes January at 10:10 (`gone` on the key, its own `at`); the desktop sets December to 60,000 at 10:05. Per key [AE1]: December goes to the newer key, the desktop's 60,000 (10:05 after 10:00); January's removal (10:10) is newer than the desktop's 1 Nov key, so it stays removed [M3]. The record goes to the phone (10:10).

cases.question: merge
cases.title: AE1: a `plan.shares` entry's `once` set for different periods on two devices keeps both
cases.why: The phone gives Free to spend 25,000 for the period of the 25 Dec pay (10:00); the desktop puts 9,000 to the trip for the period of the 25 Jan pay (10:05). Each `once` key of a share entry carries its own `at` and `by` and merges key by key [AE1]: both stay. The entry's own fields go to the desktop (10:05).

cases.question: merge
cases.title: AE1, H6: a key removed and put back with Undo wins over the removal still on the other device
cases.why: December's 0 was removed on the phone at 10:00 (the key `gone`, its own `at`) and that synced to the desktop. At 10:02 the phone undoes the removal: the key again with no `gone` and a newer `at` [H6]. Per key the Undo (10:02) is newer than the removal (10:00) the desktop holds, so December stays 0 [AE1].

cases.question: merge
cases.title: AE1, H6: on the same `at` a removed key wins; two live keys on the same `at` go to the larger `by`
cases.why: Two devices write keys with the same `at`, 24 Nov 10:00. December: one removed it, one kept it: the removed key wins on the same `at` [H6, AE1]. January: both live, 280,000 by aaaaaa and 290,000 by bbbbbb: the larger `by` wins [L merge q1], 290,000, so both devices agree.

cases.question: merge
cases.title: AE1, AE2: the pay day answered on the phone writes January's waiting 0; a rename on the desktop before the sync keeps it
cases.why: Both devices moved the same 38.31 copy (last saved Mon 23 Nov 20:00), which holds January 2027 pay of 0 waiting for the pay day. On Sat 28 Nov 08:00 the phone answers: the 25th. That adds a `rules` entry (the answer's `at`) and writes January's 0 on the 25 Jan pay, the key carrying the entry's `at`, 23 Nov 20:00 [AE2]; the entry is kept `gone` with the answer's `at`. On Sun 29 Nov the desktop, not yet synced, renames the pay. At the merge the record goes to the desktop (29 Nov): "Salary (Acme)". The `rules` entry and the `amounts` key are only on the phone and merge by entry and by key [L merge q2, AE1], so both stay: January counts 0, not 250,000. The waiting entry: the phone's `gone` (28 Nov 08:00) is newer than the desktop's live copy (23 Nov 20:00), so it is not applied again (confirm_review_3 item 1, the worst chain).

cases.question: receive
cases.title: AE1, M4, N1: a key that arrives more than a day ahead is held, with its own mark
cases.why: This device has seen up to 24 Nov 10:00, so a day ahead is 25 Nov 10:00. A device with its clock three days fast sends the pay with December's 0 written at 27 Nov 10:00. The record and the key are each held at 24 Nov 10:00:00.001, each marked with the `at` it came with and the held one [M4, N1, AE1], and the warning is shown. Then the merge: the held record (10:00:00.001) is newer than mine (1 Nov), and the key is only in the arriving copy, so December's 0 is kept with its mark.

cases.question: restore_merge
cases.title: AE5: a restore on a device whose clock is behind stamps with the D4 clock (`nextAt`), so the merge still keeps it
cases.why: The backup (Tue 10 Nov) holds a spend of 1,000. Since then the desktop changed it to 1,500 (Wed 18 Nov 10:00) and added a spend of 2,000; the phone has seen both. The phone's clock is behind: it reads Tue 17 Nov 09:00 when the backup is restored. The restore stamps with the D4 clock [AE5]: the larger of now and the newest `at` seen plus 1 ms, 18 Nov 10:00:00.001. So the 1,000 comes back and the 2,000 is `gone` (the restore's day, 17 Nov), each with that `at`, newer than every `at` in the cloud copy, and the merge keeps the restore either way round. With the raw time (17 Nov 09:00) the desktop's 1,500 (18 Nov) would come back: only part of the restore would hold (confirm_review_3, restore column).

cases.question: restore
cases.title: AE5: a restore covers records with built ids (`set:`, `pe:`, `mv:draw:`) like any other
cases.why: The backup (Thu 26 Nov 07:00) holds the moved Emergency fund draw `mv:draw:once.2027-01` (20,000) and October's period-end answer `pe:pay@2026-10-25:free` (1,500 to Waiting). After it the desktop changed the draw to 15,000 (12:00), ticked the 25 Nov pay, writing `set:pay@2026-11-25` (12:30), and changed the answer to 2,000 (13:00). On Fri 27 Nov 09:00 the phone restores the backup [AE5]. Built ids are records like any other: the draw comes back at 20,000 and the answer at 1,500, each with the restore's `at` and `by`; the settle is not in the backup, so it is `gone` (27 Nov) with the restore's `at`, and the 25 Nov pay is expected again. `told` stays each record's first [H1].

cases.question: restore
cases.title: AE5: a restore covers `pendingMove`, the frozen texts and keyed overrides: what waited at the backup waits again
cases.why: The phone moved its 38.31 copy (last saved Mon 23 Nov 20:00) and made a backup before answering anything: January's pay of 0 waits in `pendingMove`. Later the desktop moved too (its frozen text `mv:frozen:dsk001`), and on Sat 28 Nov the phone answered the pay day, the 25th: a `rules` entry, January's 0 as `amounts` on 25 Jan, the entry `gone`. On Sun 29 Nov 09:00 the phone restores the backup [AE5]: the schedule, its step, the waiting entry and the phone's frozen text come back as the backup holds them, each with the restore's `at`. What is newer than the backup is removed by its own `gone` (29 Nov) with that `at`: the `rules` entry [M3], the `amounts` key [AE1] and the desktop's frozen text. So the pay day is asked again and January's 0 waits for it again.

cases.question: restore_merge
cases.title: AE5, N1: a restore keeps the held marks the device knows, so the fast device's copy cannot beat the restore
cases.why: A device with its clock two days fast changed a spend to 5,000, written at Thu 26 Nov 10:00. The phone, which had seen up to Tue 24 Nov 10:00, held it at 24 Nov 10:00:00.001 with the mark { came 26 Nov 10:00, at 24 Nov 10:00:00.001 } [M4, N1]. The backup (Mon 23 Nov) holds 4,000. On 24 Nov 12:00 the phone restores it [AE5]: 4,000 with the restore's `at` (12:00), and the record keeps the held mark the phone knows, as an edit keeps it [N1]. The fast device's own copy in the cloud still says 26 Nov 10:00: that is the mark's `came`, so it counts at the held 24 Nov 10:00:00.001 and the restore (12:00) wins, either way round. Without the mark the 26 Nov copy would win and the restore would not hold.

cases.question: restore_merge
cases.title: AE5, AE1: a restore covers keyed overrides key by key; the merge with the cloud copy keeps it
cases.why: The backup (Tue 24 Nov 09:00) holds December pay of 50,000 (`amounts` key 2026-12-25), the car loan with no extra and Food with no `once`. After it: December pay changed to 0 (10:00), January pay set to 100,000, 30,000 extra planned on the loan from January, and Food 70,000 for the December period (all 25 Nov). On Thu 26 Nov 09:00 the phone restores the backup [AE5]. Key by key [AE1]: December pay back to 50,000 with the restore's `at`; January's key, the January extra and Food's December key are not in the backup, so each is removed by its own `gone` (26 Nov) with the restore's `at`; the steps and the loan's first extra entry get the new `at` [M3]. Every stamp is 26 Nov 09:00, newer than the cloud copy's newest (25 Nov 10:00), so the merge keeps the restore either way round: December pay 50,000, January the usual 300,000, no extra on the loan.

cases.question: restore
cases.title: AF3: a restore writes `gone` for a shared `ui` key not in the backup
cases.why: The backup (Tue 10 Nov) holds askNums true. After it the desktop set askNums false (15 Nov) and a new key, hideTips true (16 Nov). On Sat 21 Nov 09:00 the phone restores the backup: askNums takes the backup's true with a new `at` [AD8]; hideTips is not in the backup, so it is removed by its own `gone` in `ui.gone` (the restore's day) with the restore's `at` and `by` [AF3]. Nothing is deleted: its value stays beside the mark (section 0), and the screen reads a `gone` key as not set.

cases.question: restore_merge
cases.title: AF3: the merge with the cloud copy keeps the restored `ui` key removed, on either side
cases.why: The cloud copy still has hideTips true at 16 Nov 10:00 with no `gone`. The restored key is `gone` at 21 Nov 09:00, newer, so it wins per key [AF3, L merge q6]; askNums as in mg-99. Merged either way round it is the restored `ui`. Before AF3 the restore left the key out and the cloud's hideTips came back at the next sync (mg-q13).

cases.question: merge
cases.title: AF3, H6: a removed `ui` key wins on the same `at`; a key put back with Undo wins when newer
cases.why: hideTips: removed by aaaaaa and kept by bbbbbb, both at 21 Nov 09:00. On the same `at` the removed key wins, before `by` [H6, AF3]: it stays removed. askNums: removed by aaaaaa at 10:00 and put back with Undo by bbbbbb at 10:05, newer, so it is set again, with no `gone`.

cases.question: merge
cases.title: AE2, AE1: a key the person edited after one device applied the waiting entry wins over the same key another device applies later
cases.why: Both devices moved the copy (last saved 23 Nov 20:00), January's 0 waiting. The desktop answered the pay day on Thu 26 Nov 08:00, applied the entry (January 0, the key at 23 Nov 20:00) and on Fri 27 Nov 10:00 the person changed January to 120,000 there (unpaid leave cancelled; the key at 27 Nov 10:00). The phone, offline, answered on Sat 28 Nov 08:00 and applied its own copy of the entry: January 0, the key at the entry's `at`, 23 Nov 20:00 [AE2]. At the merge the key is judged by its own `at` [AE1]: the desktop's 120,000 (27 Nov) is newer than the phone's 0 (23 Nov), so January counts 120,000. The record goes to the phone (28 Nov 08:00); the `rules` entries from the 22nd are one entry, the phone's newer; the entry is `gone` on both, the phone's newer kept.

cases.question: restore
cases.title: AE5: a 38.31-format backup restored after the move is moved, and every record it gives is stamped with the restore
cases.why: The phone moved its 38.31 copy (last saved Mon 23 Nov 10:00, its `rev` time), so every moved record carries 23 Nov 10:00 [AB1]. Then: the pay day answered and the pay renamed (Wed 25 Nov 10:00), the moved receipt changed to 1,500 (11:00), a spend of 2,000 added (Thu 26 Nov). On Fri 27 Nov 09:00 the person restores a backup file in the 38.31 format, the same copy as before the move. The restore runs the move on it [AE5] (the currency asked again: JPY) and stamps every record it gives with the restore's `at`, 27 Nov 09:00, and `by`; stamped with the copy's last save (23 Nov) they would lose to every edit since. So: the pay is "Salary" again with its step at the restore's `at`; its `rules` entry is not in the backup, so it is removed by its own `gone` (27 Nov) [M3] and the pay day is asked again; the receipt is 1,200 again; the opening and the check are the backup's; the 2,000 spend is `gone` (27 Nov) [AB watch]. `told` stays each record's first [H1].

cases.question: restore
cases.title: AE5: a restore covers every kind of record alike: each event kind, built ids, a bill, a place and each account kind
cases.why: The backup (Fri 20 Nov 10:00) holds one record of each kind: the bank's opening with a `notYet` item, a refund, a transfer and its fee record `fee:<transfer id>`, a repay, a borrow, a convert, an adjust, a move between places, a filler, a skip `skip:gym@2026-11-19`, a period start `ps:pay@2026-11-25`, a removed place's move `rm:trip`, a closing's transfer `close:cash`, the rent bill with its step, the trip place, a card and a cash account. On Wed 25 Nov 10:00 the desktop changed each of them (an amount, a name, a day, the opening's `notYet`), and added a refund, a skip, a closing `close:card`, a place and an e-wallet. On Fri 27 Nov 09:00 the phone restores the backup [AE5]: each record the backup holds comes back as the backup holds it, with the restore's `at` and `by` (the rent's step too) [AB watch, M3]; each record added after it is removed by its own `gone` (27 Nov) with that `at`. The restore never looks at a record's kind or how its id was made, so the merge keeps it for each of them as in mg-97. `told` stays each record's first [H1].

cases.question: merge
cases.title: AG1: January's 0 written again after a restore wins at the merge over the cloud copy that holds the restore's removal
cases.why: The phone's copy of mv-117 (the pay day answered again at Sun 29 Nov 10:00) meets the cloud copy, which took the phone's restore at 09:00 (mg-111) and nothing since. The schedule: the phone's `at` 10:00 is newer than 09:00, so its record wins [D4]. Inside it, the `rules` entry from 22 Nov: the phone's live entry at 10:00 against the cloud's removed one at 09:00: the newer wins [M3], live. The `amounts` key 2027-01-25: the phone's 0 at 10:00 against the cloud's removal at 09:00: newer wins [AE1], so the 0 stays and January counts 0 on both devices. Had the key carried the entry's `at` (09:00, the restore's), the cloud's removal would win on the same `at` [H6] (mv-q56). The step from 22 Nov is the same on both (09:00, phn001). The waiting entry: the phone's `gone` at 10:00 is newer than the cloud's live copy at 09:00, so it is gone on both and never applied a third time. The frozen texts are the same on both (the desktop's removed by the restore). `told` stays each record's first [H1].
